item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I can't believe that this made me empathize with 106. Not just that, it actually made me feel bad for him.
I really like that it uses a different approach than most 106 tales, which usually portray him as nothing more than a sadistic reality-bending predator. Here, he's not evil. He's the last of an ancient species, starving to death while trying to navigate a world that changes faster then he can process it.
It does have some parts that conflict with the main article, but it was so well-written and surprisingly-emotional that I don't even mind the conflicts in canons.
+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I choose to believe that this is 106 before he really gets into the swing of things at the Foundation. I mean, from what I gather his food supply has thinned out on the outside…now the chickens have invited him into the roost. Why wouldn't he stay? And assuming that he is 'weak' in this tale because he is starving…certainly he'll become a bigger handful when he is no longer starving.

In short (and for me, at least), it makes him slightly less psychopathic-serial-killer SCP and a lot more humanoid apex predator adapting to his new hunting grounds. And that's pretty nifty. If I had cookies, I'd give you one. Instead have my upvote <3

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I saw it more as a bit of perspective; in his seemingly ageless (to us) state, a quick hunt would take days, a brief hesitation before grabbing prey would be hours of staring, etc. In his perspective, a single person coming up and smacking him with a two by four would be annoying, but a full security patrol shooting at him would be like being attacked by a hive of hornets before you even realized you had disturbed them.

And yeah, I can definitely sympathize, but only in the same way as one sympathizes with a shark; you know it's a predator, you know it's just doing what it does, but you do not want to be on the business end of those teeth!

item.content:encoded: Cheers - the dimensional stuff is definitely there (e.g. the mention of burrowing through moats and 'moving over and through' the earth), though I wanted to make it seem, at least at first, as though it were just part of his dementia. I agree with the frailty thing and I've revised it somewhat - especially a bit that in retrospect stood out for me where I have him afraid of falling. Hopefully what's left doesn't jar too much with what we know from the article - e.g. that he is dazed and weakened by bright light.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is extremely well written, but I feel like elements of the source are lost in translation. The spacetime pockets are at the top of the list, along with the tortuously slow and sadistic methods of playing with it's food. The frailty we see here is also somewhat at odds with the difficulty we have dealing with him during his hunting cycle- I feel like I could fend this version off with a two by four quickly enough to feel bad about breaking its hip.

All that said, upvote. It's a fascinating take, and the writing is spot on.
